patients.label: 60-year-old female patient with chest pain and LAD stenosis who developed longitudinal stent compression during stent placement
attribution_limitations: Source conflict: the case text gives approximately 70% stenosis of the narrowest portion and medial segment of the left circumflex (LCX) artery and cites Fig. 1A for it, while the Fig. 1A caption describes the 70% type A lesion as being in the medial LAD. The same lesion is given two different vessels. Panel A prints only the vessel labels "LCX" and "LAD", with no percentage or arrow. The text separately gives a long LAD stenosis.

The case presentation names 2.5 × 28 mm and 3.0 × 16 mm Element stents and the abstract states that 2 stents were implanted, while the discussion states that the Promus stent was also used in the case reported here. No third stent is described; the source does not state whether "Promus" refers to the Element stents.

Several balloons are described for the post-stent steps: a 3.5 × 12 mm Voyager NC post-dilation balloon, an unnamed "another balloon" maneuvered past the proximal stent, the balloon that post-dilated the overlapping stents, and a 3.5 × 8 mm GRIP balloon. The source does not state which of these are the same balloon or the order of the abstract-level "another balloon" step relative to the GRIP dilation.

The case text says the balloon "had to be withdrawn"; the source states the guidewire adjustment and the later passage of another balloon but gives no separate completed-action wording for the withdrawal.

claims.text: A 60-year-old female patient with a 7-year history of chest pain and no history of hypertension or diabetes was hospitalized after 2 months of exacerbated pain. Electrocardiography showed no significant ischemic changes. Selective coronary angiography revealed a long stenosis in the proximal to medial segment of the LAD, with fractional flow reserve values of 0.87 and 0.76 for the LCX and LAD and a 13 mmHg pressure gradient in the medial LAD.

Radiography and IVUS showed stent malapposition, longitudinal stent compression at the proximal stent opening, overlapping and poor stent adherence.
